setting: the same cozy kid bedroom at night in every picture: a low wooden bed with a lavender blanket and a soft white pillow against the left wall, soft warm peach walls, a window in the middle of the back wall showing a dark blue night sky with a crescent moon and a few stars, a small warm glowing lamp on a little wooden shelf on the back wall between the bed and the window, a soft round cream rug in the middle of the wooden floor, and a rounded light-wood door on the right wall with a big upright teal grown-up suitcase (handle, little wheels, small red heart tag) standing on the floor just left of the door. Props look the same in every picture: the little backpack is a small rounded soft-orange kid backpack with a yellow star on its front pocket and two straps; the sun hat is a round straw hat with a wide brim and a pink ribbon; the water bottle is light blue with a white cap; the sand bucket is a small red pail with a handle and a little yellow spade; the clothes are a light-blue t-shirt and yellow shorts; the toys are a few colorful wooden blocks and a small red-and-white ball. Few props, soft warm light, gentle shadows. The bottom-right corner of the picture is plain wooden floor with nothing important in it

props_trip.note: Draw only the twelve things listed, no child. The four backpacks are the very same backpack the child holds in the attached sheet: same orange, same front pocket, same yellow star, same straps and top handle. No faces on anything. Every thing is seen from the same angle: from the front, slightly from above. The four backpacks are the very same backpack at the same size and angle; only its shape and what is in it change. The two hats are the very same round straw sun hat with a wide brim and a pink ribbon. The three clothes figures are the very same light-blue t-shirt and yellow shorts. Sizes compared with the empty backpack: the suitcase is about three times as tall; the water bottle and the sand bucket are each about half as tall; the hat is about as wide; the flat t-shirt and shorts together are about as wide; the crumpled ball of clothes is about two thirds as wide; the folded stack is about half as wide and low and flat. The ball and each block sticking out of the bulging backpack are about one third of the backpack's width.
